decisive_items: skin thickening over the last 5 years
Capillaroscopy Image Description: Late signs with avascular areas
response.rationale: Systemic sclerosis best explains the combination of skin thickening, Raynaud phenomenon, salt-and-pepper lesions, interstitial lung disease, pulmonary hypertension, capillaroscopy with avascular areas, and dysphagia. Other candidates explain only subsets such as sicca, arthritis, or serositis.

rejected.why: Anti-Sm, ANA, low C3, and serositis are present, but the skin thickening, Raynaud phenomenon, ILD, pulmonary hypertension, and capillaroscopy changes are not explained by SLE.
Arthritis, morning stiffness, and elevated inflammatory markers are present, but the scleroderma-specific skin, vascular, pulmonary, and capillaroscopy features are absent.

Ocular dryness, dysgeusia, and abnormal Schirmer test support Sjögren's syndrome, but this does not account for skin thickening, Raynaud phenomenon, ILD, pulmonary hypertension, or capillaroscopy changes.

MCTD could explain some overlap features, but anti-Sm and low C3 are atypical, and the systemic sclerosis-specific skin thickening, salt-and-pepper lesions, and avascular capillaroscopy pattern dominate the presentation.
